original_question: For each dimension d>=3, let r(d) be the smallest positive integer for which there exists a 1-factorization of the d-dimensional hypercube Q_d such that the union of any r(d) distinct 1-factors is connected. Determine the value of r(d).
target_in_paper: arXiv:2310.18163, Section 2 ("Connecting factors of the hypercube"), Question 2.1 (Behague, [1]); this same problem is repeated in the later dedicated paper arXiv:2508.15698 as Question 1.1.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object and quantifiers almost verbatim: the d-dimensional hypercube Q_d, the parameter r(d), the range d >= 3, the existential quantifier over 1-factorizations of Q_d, and the requirement that the union of any r(d) distinct factors be connected. This is essentially the same problem as the paper's official formulation.
missing_details: Q_d should be defined explicitly as the graph on {0,1}^d whose edges join vertices that differ in exactly one coordinate.
The term '1-factorization' should be defined explicitly as a partition of E(Q_d) into perfect matchings (equivalently, into d 1-factors).
It should be made explicit that the r(d) factors are chosen from one fixed 1-factorization, not from different factorizations.

The phrase 'the union of any r(d) distinct 1-factors' should be formalized as: for every subset N of the chosen factorization with |N| = r(d), the spanning subgraph obtained by taking the union of the matchings in N is connected.
It is helpful to say that the union is a graph-theoretic union of edge sets on the full vertex set V(Q_d).
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency hypotheses are involved here; the only missing data are graph-theoretic definitions and quantifier clarifications.
refined_question: For each integer d >= 3, let Q_d be the d-dimensional hypercube graph on vertex set {0,1}^d, with two vertices adjacent when they differ in exactly one coordinate. A 1-factorization of Q_d is a partition of E(Q_d) into d perfect matchings. Define r(d) to be the least positive integer for which there exists a 1-factorization M of Q_d such that, for every subfamily N ⊆ M with |N| = r(d), the spanning subgraph obtained by taking the union of the matchings in N is connected. Determine the exact value of r(d).
justification: The draft is already very close to the official statement in the paper: arXiv:2310.18163 states essentially this problem as Question 2.1. The only substantive improvements needed are to make the graph Q_d and the notion of 1-factorization explicit and to replace the informal phrase 'any r(d) distinct 1-factors' by the unambiguous subfamily formulation. I did not broaden the problem to semi-perfect or k-semi-perfect factorizations, nor to the later random-factorization conjecture. The nearby context in Section 2 of arXiv:2310.18163, especially Lemma 2.2, supplies the paper's intended connectivity setting and the fact that the r(d)=2 case is impossible. The later dedicated paper arXiv:2508.15698 repeats the same question in its introduction and uses exactly the subset-of-factors language adopted in the refined rewrite.
